prompt: In a carbonyl condensation reaction, what kind of reaction does the nucleophilic (donor) partner undergo?

choices.why: That is what happens to the electrophilic partner, whose carbonyl group is attacked by the enolate ion.
The section describes the condensation as a combination of nucleophilic addition and α-substitution steps; the donor reacts at its α carbon.
The donor is converted into an enolate ion and bonds through its α carbon to the second partner, which is an α substitution.

explanation: One partner is converted into an enolate-ion nucleophile and adds to the electrophilic carbonyl group of the second partner. The nucleophilic partner undergoes an α-substitution reaction, and the electrophilic partner undergoes a nucleophilic addition (Figure 23.1.1).

prompt: After protonation, what kind of product does an aldol reaction give?

choices.why: The new bond joins the α carbon of one partner to the carbonyl carbon of the other, so the –OH ends up on the β carbon, not the α carbon.
The –OH is one carbon closer than that: it sits on the β carbon, giving the two oxygens a 1,3 relationship.
Only one carbonyl group becomes an alcohol; the other carbonyl group stays in the product.

explanation: The aldol reaction bonds the α carbon of one partner to the carbonyl carbon of the second. After protonation the product is a β-hydroxy carbonyl compound, so the two oxygen atoms have a 1,3 relationship.

prompt: What is the aldol product formed when acetaldehyde, CH3CHO, is treated with sodium hydroxide in ethanol?

choices.why: The –OH comes from the acceptor's carbonyl oxygen, which ends up on the β carbon (carbon 3), not on carbon 2.
That would put the oxygens in a 1,4 relationship. In an aldol product they are 1,3.
Both partners are aldehydes; the aldehyde group of the donor stays an aldehyde in the product.

explanation: Treatment of acetaldehyde with a base such as sodium ethoxide or sodium hydroxide in a protic solvent gives 3-hydroxybutanal, known as aldol (aldehyde + alcohol). This compound gives the reaction its name.

prompt: What is the aldol product of propanal, CH3CH2CHO, in base (Worked Example 23.1.1)?

choices.why: The new bond forms at the α carbon of propanal, which carries a methyl group, so the product has a methyl branch on carbon 2.
In an aldol product the –OH is on the β carbon, giving a 1,3 relationship between the oxygens, not 1,2.
That product has only five carbons. Two propanal molecules give a six-carbon product.

explanation: The α carbon (carbon 2) of one propanal bonds to the carbonyl carbon of a second propanal. After protonation, the product is 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal, a β-hydroxy aldehyde.

prompt: What is the aldol product of butanal, CH3CH2CH2CHO (Exercise 23.1.1)?

choices.why: The α carbon of butanal carries an ethyl group, so the product branches at carbon 2; it isn't a straight chain.
The –OH comes from the acceptor carbonyl and ends up on the β carbon (carbon 3), not on carbon 2.
That has only six carbons. Two molecules of butanal give a product with eight.

explanation: The α carbon of one butanal (which carries an ethyl group) bonds to the carbonyl carbon of a second butanal. The product, CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CH(CH2CH3)CHO, is 2-ethyl-3-hydroxyhexanal.

prompt: Acetophenone, C6H5COCH3, has eight carbon atoms. How many carbon atoms does its aldol product contain?
explanation: An aldol reaction combines two molecules of reactant and loses nothing, so the product has 2 × 8 = 16 carbons. It is C6H5COCH2C(OH)(CH3)C6H5 (Exercise 23.1.1b).

prompt: Which of these compounds can't undergo an aldol reaction with itself?

choices.why: Acetaldehyde has α hydrogens and gives 3-hydroxybutanal, the original aldol.
Cyclohexanone has α hydrogens; the section shows it giving a β-hydroxy ketone (22% at equilibrium).
Phenylacetaldehyde has α hydrogens and gives its β-hydroxy aldehyde in 90% yield.

explanation: Only aldehydes and ketones with an α hydrogen atom undergo the aldol reaction, because one partner must be converted into an enolate ion. In 2,2-dimethylpropanal the α carbon is bonded to three methyl groups and has no hydrogen.

prompt: For which kind of carbonyl compound does the aldol equilibrium generally favor the condensation product?

choices.text: Aldehydes with no α substituent, RCH2CHO

choices.why: For these the equilibrium favors the reactant, because the extra substitution crowds the aldol product.
For most ketones the equilibrium favors the reactant; cyclohexanone gives only 22% of its β-hydroxy ketone.
The position of the equilibrium depends on substrate structure, so it differs from compound to compound.

explanation: The aldol equilibrium favors the product for aldehydes with no α substituent (RCH2CHO) but favors the reactant for disubstituted aldehydes (R2CHCHO) and most ketones. Steric factors are probably responsible: more substitution near the reaction site means more crowding in the aldol product.

prompt: At equilibrium, phenylacetaldehyde gives 90% of its β-hydroxy aldehyde, while cyclohexanone gives only 22% of its β-hydroxy ketone. How many percentage points higher is the value for phenylacetaldehyde?
explanation: 90% − 22% = 68 percentage points. Phenylacetaldehyde is an RCH2CHO aldehyde, for which the equilibrium favors the product, while for most ketones, such as cyclohexanone, it favors the reactant.

prompt: The base-catalyzed reverse-aldol reaction of 4-hydroxy-4-methyl-2-pentanone, (CH3)2C(OH)CH2COCH3, gives what (Exercise 23.1.2)?

choices.why: Those two contain only five carbons in all; 4-hydroxy-4-methyl-2-pentanone has six.
Two propanal molecules give 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal, a β-hydroxy aldehyde, not this β-hydroxy ketone.
Those two contain seven carbons in all; the starting compound has six.

explanation: The aldol reaction is reversible. 4-Hydroxy-4-methyl-2-pentanone is the aldol product of acetone, so the reverse reaction, the exact opposite of the forward reaction, breaks it into 2 equivalents of acetone.
